subject: Estimation of variance components depends on magnitude?

messages.author: 6e50d514a7c719fe
messages.subject: Estimation of variance components depends on magnitude?
parts:
Hello,
I'm super excited about using stan, so thanks up front to all those who helped develop it. I've noticed something that I can't quite figure out. Basically, in estimating a random intercept model the estimation of the second-level variance seems to depend strongly on the magnitude of this variance. At least, that's what I think is going on (always a possibility of user error!). An example is pasted at the bottom. In each iteration, I keep the second-level SD twice that of the first-level. In the first iteration, the base-level SD is 5 which gets correctly recovered by stan. In the second iteration, the base-level SD is 150. This really throws stan off. Any explanations? I came across this trying to replicate some prior results and was able to do so once I rescaled things, but it was quite puzzling at first. 

Ben Domingue

#START EXAMPLE
library(lme4)
library(rstan)
set.seed(50050)
nf<-1000
ind_per_fam<-3
ni<-nf*ind_per_fam

code<-"
  data {
    int ni;
    int nf;
    real y[ni];
    int gr[ni];
  }
  parameters {
    real b_int;
    real<lower=0> s1;
    real<lower=0> s2;
    real r1[nf];
  }
  model {
    #priors for params
    b_int~normal(0,1000);
    s1~uniform(0,1000);
    s2~uniform(0,1000);
    #random effects
    for (n in 1:nf)
      r1[n]~normal(0,s2);
    #finally data
    for (n in 1:ni) {
      y[n]~normal(b_int+r1[gr[n]],s1);
    }
  }
"

out.stan<-out.lmer<-list()
for (base.var in c(5,150)) {
  gr<-rep(1:nf,ind_per_fam)
  fam.eff<-rnorm(nf,sd=base.var*2)
  err<-rnorm(ni,sd=base.var)
  y<-fam.eff[gr]+err
  #
  lmer(y~(1|gr))->out.lmer[[as.character(base.var)]]
  #
  fit <- stan(model_code = code, data = list(ni=ni,nf=nf,y=y,gr=gr), iter = 1000, n_chains = 1)
  summary(fit)$summary[,1]->S
  grepl("r[123]",names(S))->index
  S[!index]->out.stan[[as.character(base.var)]]
}
#END EXAMPLE

As a brief follow-up, I am getting better results with 3000 iterations. This somewhat surprises me given that the variances are always within the range of the prior... 

Ben

n 9/6/12 1:05 PM, Ben Domingue wrote:
> As a brief follow-up, I am getting better results with 3000 iterations. This somewhat surprises me given that the
> variances are always within the range of the prior...

After it converges, do you get decent effective
sample sizes? If so, I'm guessing the problem is
in initialization.

That's a very fat uniform prior on the
variances, which doesn't provide much guidance.

With a range of [0,1000], the initial values Stan
generates randomly will be centered around 500. It
can take a while to settle from overly high variances,
especially with the dependence in hierarchical models.

One tack you can take if you must have such a wide
prior is to provide more reasonable initializations
by hand.

- Bob

Thanks Bob. The more I think about this I'm seeing that it isn't all that surprising. I suppose another approach would be to modify the step size. Or, even better, to be more careful with the range of the DV!

Thanks again,
Ben
